hypotheses.null: Mean connector rate is equal across AI and human documents.
hypotheses.statement: Connector rate (however/therefore/moreover/additionally/overall/furthermore per token) is higher in AI-generated text than in human text.

hypotheses.null: The distributions of token entropy are equal across AI and human documents.
hypotheses.statement: Token entropy (Shannon entropy over word tokens) is lower in AI-generated text than in human text.

hypotheses.null: Adding unique_ratio to a logistic model containing log_words does not improve fit (likelihood-ratio test, df=1).
hypotheses.statement: Unique-token ratio discriminates AI from human text beyond document length.

hypotheses.null: All family centroids are equal (one-way MANOVA, Wilks' lambda, permutation p-value).
hypotheses.statement: Per-family feature centroids (connectors, unique_ratio, long_words, token_entropy) are separated across source families, including human.

hypotheses.null: Mean long-word rate is equal across AI and human text documents.
hypotheses.statement: Long-word rate (fraction of tokens with >= 7 characters) is higher in AI prose than in human prose.

hypotheses.null: Durbin-Watson statistic on document-ordered segment residuals is consistent with no positive autocorrelation.
hypotheses.statement: Segment-level detector residuals are uncorrelated within documents (the segment-independence assumption holds).
